title: Stop a Dripping Faucet
summary: That drip is money and wear. Usually a washer or cartridge — shut the water off first.

learn.heading: What you're looking at
learn.body: A dripping faucet means water is getting past the shutoff inside the handle. Compression faucets (two handles, hot and cold) use rubber washers at the stem base. Single-handle faucets often use a cartridge. Under the sink you'll find shutoff valves on the supply lines — turn clockwise to close.

learn.heading: What can hurt you
learn.body: Shut the water off before you open anything. A geyser from a live line soaks you and the cabinet. Don't force frozen valves — heat gently or call a plumber. Know where the main house shutoff is if the under-sink valves fail.
learn.callout: Take the old washer or cartridge to the hardware store. Match it, don't guess.

learn.heading: The steps
learn.body:
1. Close the shutoff valves under the sink (clockwise). Open the faucet to relieve pressure.
2. Plug the drain — small parts disappear fast.
3. Remove the handle (set screw often under a decorative cap).
4. For compression: unscrew the packing nut, pull the stem, replace the washer at the bottom, reassemble.
5. For cartridge: pull the retaining clip, remove the cartridge, replace with a match.
6. Reassemble in reverse order. Don't overtighten.
7. Turn water back on slowly. Check for leaks at the handle and spout.

practice.prompt: Put the faucet repair steps in order.

steps.text: Shut off water at the valves under the sink
Plug the drain and open the faucet to drain
Remove handle and replace washer or cartridge
Reassemble and turn water back on slowly

practice.failMessage: Water off first. Always. Then drain, fix, reassemble.

practice.prompt: Tap what you turn off before opening the faucet.
practice.failMessage: Shut the supply valves under the sink — not the aerator or trap.

practice.prompt: What's wrong with this faucet repair?

options.text: Handle removed with supply valves still open
Drain plugged so parts don't fall in
options.feedback: Plugging the drain is correct — parts are tiny.

options.text: Old washer brought to the store for matching
options.feedback: Matching the old part is exactly right.

practice.failMessage: Open supply lines while disassembling = flooded cabinet. Shut off first.
